text: Tungro (ជំងឺទង់ស្រោ) is a viral rice disease transmitted by green leafhoppers (ស្រង្កែជញ្ជក់ទឹកដោះ type / green leafhopper vector insects) rather than by direct plant-to-plant contact. Infected plants show reduced tillering, and leaves turn yellow-orange starting from the tip, often with small brownish or rust-colored speckling. In severe cases the panicle either fails to fully emerge from the flag leaf sheath, or panicles that do emerge are poorly filled or largely empty. The main practical impact is reduced tillering and poor grain fill, which shows up as lower yield at harvest. Risk rises with a nearby green leafhopper population and with poor field sanitation, such as leaving infected rice stubble or ratoon regrowth standing after harvest, which lets both the vector and the virus persist between crops. Recommended control: choose resistant varieties where available; plough and sun-dry the field immediately after harvest to destroy infected stubble and volunteer regrowth that can harbor the virus and its leafhopper vector; walk the field and remove/destroy any plants showing tungro symptoms rather than leaving them; and manage the green leafhopper vector population directly using standard leafhopper control practices, since controlling the vector is central to controlling the disease. This is a confirmed addition to the rice disease knowledge base - tungro had not previously been represented by any confirmed entry despite being one of the major regional rice virus diseases.
